question: Can residual networks be parameterized so that optimal hyperparameters and feature-learning dynamics transfer jointly across width and depth, and does that parameterization admit a coherent joint infinite-width and infinite-depth training limit?

key_findings.claim: The proposed rule combines maximal-update/mean-field width scaling with a 1/sqrt(L) multiplier on each residual branch, keeping the base learning rate and feature-learning control gamma_0 independent of width N and depth L.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 1-3 and Table 1 set hidden residual branches to (LN)^(-1/2), the readout scale to gamma_0 sqrt(N), and the learning rate to eta_0 gamma_0^2 N. The intended mechanism is that independent initialization increments accumulate diffusively over L while the strongly cross-layer-correlated gradient signal produces an order-one feature-learning drift.

key_findings.claim: The empirical evidence consistently shows aligned learning-rate optima across the tested widths and depths, but it establishes short-horizon transfer on selected vision systems rather than a general or converged performance law.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 1-4 show transfer on CIFAR-10 convolutional ResNets and Tiny ImageNet/ImageNet ViTs with SGD or muP-Adam, with and without normalization, and for warmup/cosine schedules, momentum, gamma_0, and weight decay. Most runs last 10-20 epochs, the ImageNet ResNet sweep lasts 5 epochs, and the authors explicitly say most experiments are limited to 10-20 epochs. There are no uncertainty bands for the hyperparameter sweeps or matched compute-to-convergence comparisons.

key_findings.claim: The DMFT construction gives a physics-level closed stochastic description of feature-learning dynamics in the joint limit, not a formal convergence theorem.
key_findings.evidence: Propositions 1 and 3 express preactivation and backpropagated fields as Brownian layer-time processes plus feature-learning drifts, with feature and gradient kernels and response functions determined self-consistently. Appendix F derives the same saddle-point equations by taking depth before width and argues that the limits commute throughout training. The paper explicitly qualifies the derivations as physics-level and leaves rigorous commutativity during training open.

key_findings.claim: In the lazy limit gamma_0 approaches zero, the continuum kernels freeze and the limiting NTK is computable from coupled forward and backward layer-time ODEs; this special case deliberately removes feature learning.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 2 and Appendix G.1 give the covariance ODE for H and Phi, a backward ODE for G, and K as the integral of G times Phi. Figure 6 reports O(L^-2) squared-error convergence of the initialization-averaged finite-depth NTK for sufficiently large width.

key_findings.claim: The deep-linear one-step solution is a useful exact sanity check, but it covers one sample, one gradient step, linear activations, and a Gaussian closure rather than the nonlinear training regime of the vision experiments.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 7 solves the post-update feature-kernel profile and Figure 7 matches it against width-1000 linear ResNets at increasing depth. Appendix G.2 derives the result only after imposing linear activations and a one-sample one-step setting; the general nonlinear DMFT is said to require non-Gaussian integration or Monte Carlo.

key_findings.claim: The finite-size analysis predicts distinct error sources: order-one-in-depth finite-width fluctuations of squared scale O(N^-1), mean finite-width bias O(N^-2) in squared error, and infinite-width finite-depth discretization error O(L^-2) in squared error.
key_findings.evidence: Appendices H-I expand around the DMFT saddle, derive an O(N^-1) NTK variance independent of L, and decompose predictor error in Equations 112-116. Figure 5 and Figure B.7 report O(L^-1) expected squared error when random finite-depth variation dominates and a faster trend consistent with O(L^-2) after averaging 15 initializations.

key_findings.claim: The paper's extension to multi-layer residual blocks does not make every internal transformation learn nontrivially in the infinite-depth limit, which limits how directly the theory explains modern Transformer blocks.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix K.2 keeps the number of transformations per block fixed while L grows. It concludes that intermediate within-block gradient fields decorrelate, making the internal weights effectively lazy in the limiting equations, and explicitly leaves reparameterizing them for order-one depthwise feature learning as future work. Later CompleteP work targets exactly this all-layer non-laziness issue.

anchors.section: K.2 multiple layers per residual block

key_findings.claim: The exact arXiv v2 formulas contain several material boundary and indexing inconsistencies, so the intended DMFT must be reconstructed from repeated equations rather than copied from Proposition 3 alone.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 3 integrates the backward feature-learning drift from 0 to tau, whereas Equations 60 and 88 integrate the backward recursion from tau to 1, matching its terminal boundary at layer time 1. Equation 60 starts with the tautology g(tau)=g(tau)+..., Equation 51 defines C_h twice where the second line is later used as C_g, and the last response derivative in Equation 67 uses C_h where the corresponding backward relation and linear specialization use C_g. Equation 91 drops the primed input/time from both covariance products, and Equation 99 drops y^2 even though Equations 7 and 98 include it.

key_findings.claim: The ICLR supplementary artifact substantially improves reproducibility but is incomplete and contains an immediately broken default training route.
key_findings.evidence: The official ICLR 2024 supplementary ZIP (SHA-256 fe28ad373e4ca76d0a1b4052197843930f833814fc22871d4f00d82b8ce58b4b) contains eight Python files, 48 muP base-shape files, and three executed notebooks. All Python files compile, and the code supplies the omitted ViT patch sizes: 4 for CIFAR-10 and 8 for Tiny ImageNet. It has no README, license, locked environment, tests, checkpoints, metrics, or plotting scripts. In get_model, the resnet18/ImageNet branch is followed by a separate if/elif chain whose final else raises ValueError, so the parser's default arch=resnet18,dataset=imgnet route cannot return its constructed model; train also resets batches_seen to zero each epoch, defeating its cross-epoch max_updates counter.

anchors.section: G exactly solvable cases represented by supplementary notebooks

key_findings.claim: Two smaller presentation contradictions affect experimental reconstruction but do not overturn the plotted transfer trends.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix A.4 ends the sentence 'For ViTs, we use a patch size' without a value. In Figure B.3, the prose and subfigure labels/files compare epochs 3 and 9, but the caption says epochs 3 and 5. Appendix B.1 also refers to panel (a) twice when distinguishing same-width and same-depth curves.

method.core_idea: Scale each residual branch by 1/sqrt(depth) while using maximal-update width scaling, then analyze training as a self-consistent stochastic process over continuous layer time.
method.mechanism: At fixed depth, a DMFT path integral replaces neuron populations by single-site stochastic preactivation and gradient fields coupled through feature, gradient, and response kernels. Taking depth to infinity turns independent residual initialization increments into Brownian motions and correlated feature-learning updates into deterministic drifts. The resulting kernels determine a dynamic NTK and prediction flow. The reverse order of limits is examined through the infinite-depth action, and lazy and deep-linear restrictions provide analytically solvable checks.
assumptions: Residual blocks use the stated 1/sqrt(L) scaling and widthwise muP/mean-field initialization and learning-rate rules.
The width and depth limits are taken with dataset size and training time remaining order one.
The DMFT saddle-point and continuum manipulations are valid despite being presented at physics rather than theorem-proof rigor.
Independent layer initializations yield Brownian increments, while skip connections preserve order-one long-range correlations in backward fields.
The number of transformations per residual block remains fixed as the number of blocks grows.
The lazy-limit calculations take gamma_0 to zero, and the exact rich-regime solution assumes linear activations and Gaussianity.
Short-horizon optimal train loss is an adequate proxy for the hyperparameters desired at full training scale.
Architectural extensions such as Adam-trained ViTs and normalized ResNets retain the scaling behavior even where the derivation directly treats gradient flow or SGD.

techniques.role: Scales residual branches as 1/sqrt(L) so initialization noise and feature-learning drift remain order one.
Uses muP/mean-field width scaling to preserve nontrivial feature updates across width.
Converts wide-network training into self-consistent stochastic single-neuron dynamics and kernel equations.
Treats normalized layer index tau=l/L as continuous time in the infinite-depth limit.
Derives concentration and response equations through an MSR generating functional and saddle point.
Freezes features to obtain a tractable continuum NTK baseline.
Uses linear activations to retain Gaussian fields and solve a one-step rich-regime kernel profile.
Expands around the DMFT saddle to separate finite-width variance, width bias, and depth discretization error.

evaluations.setting: Simplified convolutional residual network on CIFAR-10, 20 epochs, widths and depths jointly swept
evaluations.metric: Training loss versus base learning rate
evaluations.result: Figure 1 shows a stable learning-rate optimum under 1/sqrt(L)-muP while ordinary muP shifts or diverges across depth
evaluations.baseline: muP without residual depth scaling and standard parameterization in Figure B.2

evaluations.setting: ResNet-style networks with BatchNorm or LayerNorm on CIFAR-10, 20 epochs
evaluations.metric: Training loss versus learning rate across width and depth
evaluations.result: Normalization improves deep trainability, but the 1/sqrt(L) variants display more consistent optima
evaluations.baseline: Normalized muP ResNets without 1/sqrt(L) branch scaling

evaluations.setting: muP-Adam Vision Transformers on Tiny ImageNet for 20 epochs and ImageNet for 10 epochs
evaluations.metric: Training loss or accuracy versus learning rate and training dynamics
evaluations.result: Transfer is shown with or without LayerNorm and under linear warmup or warmup plus cosine decay
evaluations.baseline: Pre-LN ViT without explicit 1/sqrt(L) scaling in one Tiny ImageNet panel; no tuned contemporary ViT baseline

evaluations.setting: Simplified CIFAR-10 convolutional residual networks, 20 epochs
evaluations.metric: Loss dynamics under momentum, gamma_0, and weight-decay sweeps
evaluations.result: Curves at two depths remain aligned early in training and preserve the preferred hyperparameter region
evaluations.baseline: Cross-depth comparison only; no adaptive tuning method

evaluations.setting: ImageNet depth extrapolations of a ResNet-18-derived model without normalization, SGD momentum 0.9, batch 128, 5 epochs
evaluations.metric: Training-loss dynamics and final loss versus learning rate
evaluations.result: Figure B.6 reports aligned trajectories and a preserved optimal learning rate across tested depths
evaluations.baseline: No normalization and no long-horizon convergence baseline

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 convolutional models after 250 SGD steps, ensemble of 15 initializations
evaluations.metric: Squared logit error relative to an N=512,L=128 ensemble proxy
evaluations.result: Finite width bottlenecks convergence at small N; at large N, average squared error trends as O(L^-1), while ensemble-mean logits trend faster
evaluations.baseline: A finite proxy rather than the inaccessible exact infinite-width/depth predictor

evaluations.setting: Infinite-width ReLU residual MLP NTK at initialization
evaluations.metric: Squared error to the continuum-depth kernel
evaluations.result: Figure 6 reports O(L^-2) squared-error convergence at sufficiently large width

evaluations.setting: Width-1000 deep linear ResNets after one gradient step on one example
evaluations.metric: Feature-kernel profile across normalized layer time
evaluations.result: Increasing finite depths approach the analytic initialization and one-step profiles

evaluations.setting: Simplified CIFAR-10 convolutional networks up to nearly one billion parameters, 20 epochs, fixed learning rate 0.046
evaluations.metric: Final train loss at fixed parameter count
evaluations.result: The tested Pareto envelope favors intermediate depths around 9-12; an extrapolated power-law fit suggests depth about 30 only at much larger width

failure_modes: Without 1/sqrt(L) residual scaling, the preferred learning rate shifts with depth and sufficiently deep runs can diverge.
Standard parameterization still fails depthwise transfer even when the residual branch is scaled by 1/sqrt(L).
Normalization improves trainability but does not by itself make depthwise transfer as consistent as the proposed scaling in the reported sweeps.
For multiple transformations per residual block, intermediate transformations become lazy in the stated infinite-depth limit.
Finite width can dominate approximation error, so increasing depth alone need not approach the joint limit.
An optimum identified after a few epochs may not remain optimal after convergence, on another task, or under a different compute budget.
The self-consistent nonlinear DMFT is computationally difficult and is not solved for the experimental vision networks.
The central exact proposition contains a reversed backward integration boundary and related notation defects that can mislead an implementation.
The official supplementary training entry point raises on its default ResNet-18/ImageNet route, and its max-update counter is reset every epoch.
The artifact depends on unpinned PyTorch, torchvision, transformers, wandb, einops, and mup behavior and does not archive logs, checkpoints, or datasets.
limitations: Author-stated: the theoretical development has physics-level rather than formal mathematical rigor.
Author-stated: dataset size and optimization time do not scale jointly with width or depth.
Author-stated: most experiments run only 10-20 epochs because of computational limits.
Author-stated: it remains theoretically unexplained why optimal hyperparameters can transfer when actual losses and predictions differ across sizes.

Reviewer-identified: the nonlinear rich-regime DMFT is not numerically solved against the CNN or ViT trajectories; validation is limited to lazy kernels, a deep-linear one-step case, and finite-size proxy trends.
Reviewer-identified: most learning-rate sweep figures provide no repeated-seed uncertainty, statistical test, held-out optimum, or matched total-compute comparison.

Reviewer-identified: the ViT experiments extend beyond the directly derived optimizer/architecture setting, while Appendix K.2 shows that multi-transformation block interiors become lazy in the stated limit.
Reviewer-identified: Proposition 3, Equations 51, 60, 67, 91, and 99 contain boundary, naming, covariance-index, or missing-factor defects.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix A omits the ViT patch size and Figure B.3 contradicts itself about the later checkpoint.
Reviewer-identified: the official supplement has useful code and notebooks but no README, license, environment lock, tests, archived results, or end-to-end working default route.
open_questions: Can the joint training limit and commutation of width and depth be proved rigorously for nonlinear residual networks?
Which depth parameterization preserves non-lazy learning in every transformation of realistic multi-layer Transformer blocks?
Do hyperparameters selected after a few epochs remain optimal at convergence and under compute-optimal training schedules?
Can the nonlinear continuum DMFT be solved efficiently enough to predict real CNN and Transformer learning curves rather than only scaling orders?
How should batch size, sequence length, token horizon, data size, training duration, optimizer state, and width-depth ratio be scaled jointly?
What parameterization minimizes finite-size transfer error, rather than merely possessing a well-defined asymptotic limit?
When is 1/sqrt(L) preferable to 1/L or effective-depth-based scaling in practical multi-path architectures?
Can a reproducible benchmark compare depth-muP, CompleteP, spectral muP, effective-depth laws, and automatic optimizers at matched compute and final validation loss?
Can symbolic or executable checks catch backward-boundary and response-kernel inconsistencies before publication?
reusable_insights: Treat a transferable parameterization as a finite-size approximation problem, not only an existence-of-limit problem.
Separate independent residual noise, which accumulates diffusively, from correlated gradient drift, which accumulates as a Riemann sum.
Audit every transformation inside a residual branch: block-level stability does not imply non-lazy learning at all internal layers.
Report both the location of the hyperparameter optimum and size-conditioned loss curves with repeated-seed uncertainty.
Test early proxy selection against full-horizon rankings before claiming tuning-cost reduction.
Decompose approximation error into random finite-width variance, deterministic width bias, and depth discretization error.
State optimizer-specific scaling rules explicitly when moving from gradient flow or SGD theory to Adam-like experiments.
Ship executable configurations, locked dependencies, plotting inputs, and smoke tests alongside scaling-law papers.
Cross-check every continuum backward equation against its terminal boundary and a finite-depth recurrence.

competitive_landscape.title: Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer
competitive_landscape.difference: Tensor Programs V introduces muTransfer and verifies stable optimal hyperparameters across width for Transformer and ResNet models. The reviewed paper adds explicit residual depth scaling and a training-time DMFT limit, but its empirical horizons and artifact are much smaller than the large-model muTransfer demonstrations.

competitive_landscape.title: Width and Depth Limits Commute in Residual Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Hayou and Yang prove commutation and Gaussian covariance behavior for 1/sqrt(depth)-scaled residual networks at initialization. The reviewed work extends the target from initialization to feature-learning training dynamics, but does so with physics-level DMFT rather than an equally rigorous theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Automatic Gradient Descent: Deep Learning without Hyperparameters
competitive_landscape.difference: Automatic Gradient Descent uses architecture-aware relative updates and depth scaling to remove the learning-rate hyperparameter and evaluates fully connected and convolutional networks through ImageNet scale. The reviewed method retains ordinary optimizers and transfers a tuned base learning rate, giving a scaling-limit account but not eliminating tuning.

competitive_landscape.title: Tensor Programs VI: Feature Learning in Infinite-Depth Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Tensor Programs VI classifies block-multiplier and learning-rate depth parameterizations, identifies a unique Depth-muP for one-layer blocks, and emphasizes feature diversity and limitations for deeper blocks. The reviewed work uses DMFT, broader CNN/ViT transfer experiments, and a 1/sqrt(L) residual rule but reaches a similar internal-block laziness boundary.

competitive_landscape.title: Don't be lazy: CompleteP enables compute-efficient deep transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: CompleteP targets depthwise transfer and non-lazy learning in every layer of practical Transformer blocks, adopts different depth scalings including 1/L residual scaling, and reports 12-34 percent compute-efficiency improvements on LLM training. It directly addresses the reviewed paper's K.2 finding that internal block layers become lazy.

competitive_landscape.title: Completed Hyperparameter Transfer across Modules, Width, Depth, Batch and Duration
competitive_landscape.difference: Complete^(d) extends CompleteP across width, depth, batch size, duration, and per-module AdamW and initialization hyperparameters in LLMs. The reviewed work isolates width-depth transfer and provides a DMFT mechanism, but does not treat duration, batch, or high-dimensional per-module tuning.

competitive_landscape.title: Hyperparameter Transfer Enables Consistent Gains of Matrix-Preconditioned Optimizers Across Scales
competitive_landscape.difference: Qiu et al. derive width/depth learning-rate and weight-decay scaling for Shampoo, SOAP, and Muon, use 1/L depth scaling, and validate Llama models from 190M to 1.4B parameters. The reviewed work predates matrix-preconditioned optimizers and studies SGD/Adam on vision networks with a 1/sqrt(L) rule.

competitive_landscape.title: Hyperparameter Transfer Laws for Non-Recurrent Multi-Path Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. define graph effective depth for CNNs, ResNets, and Transformers and predict a universal -3/2 power law for the optimal learning rate. The reviewed paper instead fixes a residual parameterization so the base learning rate remains invariant and does not formulate a general multi-path graph law.

competitive_landscape.title: Spectral Condition for muP under Width-Depth Scaling
competitive_landscape.difference: Spectral muP specifies weight and update norm scaling for k-transform residual blocks, distinguishes the k=1 and k>=2 regimes, maps the condition to multiple optimizers, and validates GPT-2 models. The reviewed DMFT focuses on k=1 blocks and concedes lazy internal transformations when k is fixed above one.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Rate Transfer in Normalized Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: nuGPT modifies the normalized-transformer parameterization using alignment exponents and reports transfer across width, depth, and token horizon. The reviewed paper tests conventional Pre-LN or unnormalized ViTs only on vision data and does not treat token-horizon transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Linear Network Training Dynamics from Random Initialization: Data, Width, Depth, and Hyperparameter Transfer
competitive_landscape.difference: Bordelon and Pehlevan give a fuller large-width theory for deep linear networks with large random datasets, one-pass SGD versus data reuse, and residual 1/sqrt(depth) limits. It deepens the reviewed paper's one-sample one-step linear sanity check but remains a linear-model analysis.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A 1/sqrt(depth)-muP parameterization transfers hyperparameters jointly across width and depth and admits a feature-learning joint infinite-width/infinite-depth DMFT limit.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The exact artifact combines CIFAR-10, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet sweeps over convolutional ResNets and ViTs with a continuum layer-time DMFT, lazy-limit NTK, one-step deep-linear solution, finite-size fluctuation analysis, and optimizer/architecture extensions. Prior work already supplied muTransfer across width and 1/sqrt(depth) signal-propagation and initialization limits; concurrent Tensor Programs VI supplied a direct depth-muP classification.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the synthesis of practical joint width-depth transfer experiments with a training-time feature-learning DMFT and finite-size error decomposition for 1/sqrt(L) residual networks. The branch scaling, muP width transfer, and initialization limit are inherited, and the generality to modern multi-layer Transformer blocks is weakened by the paper's own internal-layer laziness result and by later CompleteP and spectral-muP alternatives. The theory is insightful but should be read as a physics derivation with a malformed central displayed proposition, not as a rigorous theorem.

reviewer_notes: Read all 41 pages of the exact arXiv v2 artifact, including every displayed equation, all three propositions, Figures 1-7, Figures B.1-B.8 and M.1, Table 1, references, and Appendices A-M. Rendered every PDF page and visually reconciled plots, captions, equations, and source assets against the extracted text and official LaTeX. The cached PDF is byte-identical to the current arXiv PDF on 2026-08-24; the official source archive SHA-256 is a577a4d09b66a43ff9abbdb3a74e242dc3cc7482a92ff489e2c97a396ea86e45. The work was published at ICLR 2024. Audited the official proceedings supplementary ZIP, including all eight Python files, 48 base-shape files, and three executed notebooks; syntax compilation passed, but no end-to-end training was attempted because the dependencies, datasets, and experiment logs are not pinned or bundled. Competitor titles, mechanisms, and current arXiv versions were checked against official primary records through 2026-08-24. Plot-only trends are described qualitatively, and exact rates are attributed to the paper's theoretical or caption claims rather than independently estimated from rasterized figures.
